context: Request: M&A deals where the firm actually invoked or litigated specific performance, with the papers. Rubric: 1018-00008 (Penterra/Veridian: Veridian's October 2024 demand to compel closing; draft counterclaim and status memo as proof documents), plus precision. 1022-00002 (Northgate/Ridgeline APA, a litigation-risk memo analysing a specific-performance theory) is outside the set.

runs.failure_point: It counted a second deal as one where specific performance was invoked, on the strength of an internal risk memo and correspondence.

first_error.why: After reading a second deal's litigation-risk memo and response letter at [93]-[103], which analyse a specific-performance theory without showing it was demanded or litigated, the answer asserts that deal as qualifying.
first_error.critic_note: Reviews asked to reconcile the second matter's number and to confirm its invocation, but none questioned whether it qualified.

divergence: Mixed (T0, T2 pass; T1 fails). All three runs reached the same lead matter through path searches and text scans, read its post-termination litigation papers, and also read a second matter whose risk memo analyses a specific-performance theory. They split at the write stage: T0 and T2 wrote the second matter as a near-miss and kept it there through their checks (in T0 a check review called the single-matter answer possible narrowing and the agent still kept it out); T1 wrote it as a second qualifying matter. The critic's reviews did not differ in T1's favour: no T1 review questioned the second matter's qualification, and its screening review only asked to reconcile that matter's number.
